frozen_note: FROZEN in A0 (2026-07-09). intent-proposal/v1 was DEFINED provisional in P0 (highest re-architecture risk: the router<->consumer envelope is only proven correct once a real consumer exercises it). A0 exercised it against the hand-written fixture (tests/test_proposal_fixture.py) AND a breadth battery over the consumer-shaped fixture catalog (tests/test_proposal_exercise.py), and AWA — the first real consumer — exercised it end-to-end over its REAL catalog via the cross-repo seam test (KleinPerkins/awa consumer/tests/test_consumer_seam.py). With the envelope proven, the 11-key required floor + the enum floors are now immutable-within-v1; new fields must be OPTIONAL (see deferred_additions) and enums may only EXTEND. The freeze checker now locks status=frozen + a frozen date + freeze_exempt=false for this contract.
owner: interface (router emits; consumer reads; never persisted to a shared repo)
rationale: The proposal is the ONLY thing the router hands back: which verb, which params, from what start point, how safe, how confident, the verdict, the plain reasons, what is missing, and whether the operator must confirm. It is executionless by construction (there is no field that runs anything). The verdict is the safety-relevant output (L2). This shape is DEFINED so R-core can serialize against it, but PROVISIONAL until A0.

A0.note: Pins which catalog version produced the proposal. Recorded here as the additive-within-v1 proof (validated by tests/test_additive_compat.py + additive-manifest.json) and added to optional_keys when a consumer first needs it; freezing the 11-key required floor does NOT require adding it, and the A0 seam test pins contract-version strings, not a per-proposal echo. Additive OPTIONAL key.

R2.note: Records whether L3 LLM rerank participated; deterministic floor (L0-L2+L5) still produces a valid proposal with this absent. Additive OPTIONAL key.

excluded_by_design.consequence_descriptor: DELIBERATELY NOT a proposal field (KI4 hygiene). The kernel consequence descriptor {destroys_unshared_work, irreversible, affects_shared_ref} that drives consequence-confirmation copy is read by the consumer FROM THE KERNEL DISPOSITION at confirm time — never relayed through the router. Putting it in the router-emitted proposal would let a router artifact appear to source a safety-relevant confirmation (KI4 says confirmations are kernel-sourced). The A0 seam test MUST assert confirmation copy derives from the kernel disposition and IGNORES any router-relayed field even if present. The plan's proposal schema does not list it; it stays excluded now that the envelope is frozen (adding it later would be a v2).

additive_note: FROZEN in A0 (see frozen_note). The 11-key required floor above is now immutable-within-v1 and the enum floors only EXTEND — a removal/rename/retype of a required key needs a v2 bump (asserted by checks/intent-contract-freeze.sh). The deferred_additions above are the anticipated A0/R2 fields and are all OPTIONAL/enum-extension (additive); recording them is the additive-compatibility proof for the frozen envelope (validated by tests/test_additive_compat.py). NOTE (KI4): the kernel consequence_descriptor is intentionally EXCLUDED from this envelope (see excluded_by_design) — the consumer reads it from the kernel disposition at confirm time, not from the router.
